title: Working at Redwood: roles, career ladders, benefits, hiring & onboarding, and internal tools
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview

Purpose: This page is the canonical employee-facing handbook entry that summarizes what it’s like to work at Redwood, explains role families and career ladders, highlights benefits and perks, describes our hiring and onboarding process, and provides links and short instructions for the most used internal tools. It is intended for new hires, managers, and people-ops partners.

Audience: new employees, hiring managers, people-ops, and engineering leaders.

=== Working at Redwood ===

Redwood Inference is an engineering-first company focused on building a high-performance inference platform. Our culture values psychological safety, measured risk-taking, data-informed decisions, and customer-centric craftsmanship. We expect:

- Clear ownership and documented work.
- Regular asynchronous updates (weekly check-ins in Slack and the team docs page).
- Respectful feedback given in 1:1s and performance cycles.
- Cross-team collaboration: product, infra, research, and support.

Core principles:
- Ship small, iterate fast: short experiments + rigorous postmortems.
- Production-first thinking: reliability, observability, and cost-conscious design.
- Empathy for users: internal and external developers are treated as first-class customers.

=== Roles & Career Ladders ===

Role families (high level): engineering, product, design, research/applied-ml, SRE/infra, data, people-ops, finance, legal, customer-success, go-to-market. Each family has defined levels and competency expectations. Managers coordinate leveling with people-ops during hiring and promotion cycles.

Example engineering ladder (summary):
- E1 (IC1) — New grad / early engineer: learns codebase, completes small tickets, demonstrates curiosity.
- E2 (IC2) — Intermediate: owns components, writes reliable code, participates in design reviews.
- E3 (Senior) — Owns services or major subsystems, mentors others, influences architecture.
- E4 (Staff) — Cross-team technical scope, leads large projects, sets technical direction for multiple teams.
- E5 (Principal) — Company-level technical strategy, high-impact systems design, external representation.

Promotion process (high level):
1. Candidate works with manager to prepare a promotion packet (summary of work, impact, feedback).
2. Manager submits packet to people-ops and panel reviewers.
3. Calibration and final decision occur within 2–6 weeks depending on cycle.

Expectations & competencies (typical):
- Technical depth: code quality, design, trade-offs.
- Execution impact: shipping, cross-team coordination, measurable outcomes.
- Leadership & mentorship: coaching, hiring, org influence.
- Communication: clear written design docs and API contracts.

=== Benefits & Perks ===

Redwood’s benefits are designed to support health, financial security, and work-life balance. The list below summarizes the primary offerings; full policy pages are linked from Benefits in the People Ops space.

Health & wellness:
- Medical, dental, and vision coverage (US plans with employer contribution tiers; EMEA equivalents provided via local vendors).
- Mental health: 8 therapy sessions per year reimbursed, plus employee assistance program (EAP).
- Wellness stipend: $200/year for home gym, classes, or equipment.

Time off & flexibility:
- Unlimited PTO policy with manager coordination and a recommended minimum of 18 working days per year.
- Parental leave: primary caregiver 18 weeks; secondary caregiver 8 weeks (paid).
- Flexible hours and partial remote work by default; core collaboration hours are 10:00–15:00 (local timezone) for most teams.

Financial & retirement:
- Competitive equity grants on hire and refresh cycles.
- 401(k) matching (US) up to 4% after eligibility period.
- Annual salary review and promotion cycles.

Learning & development:
- $2,000 learning allowance per year.
- Internal mentorship program and quarterly technical workshops.

Office & equipment:
- Choice of laptop (Mac or Linux dev workstation) and $500 home office stipend on hire.
- Hybrid office model: team-level in-office days and collaboration weeks.

Other perks:
- Monthly wellness and social stipends.
- Commuter benefit or regional equivalent where available.

How to run benefits exceptions: Submit a Benefits Exception Request ticket in the People Ops service portal with justification; People Ops will triage within 5 business days.

=== Hiring & Onboarding Overview ===

High-level goals: reduce time-to-productivity, set clear role expectations, and build relationships early. Typical timeline: offer signed → week 0 (pre-boarding) → week 1 (orientation) → week 2–12 (ramp & 90-day milestones).

Pre-boarding checklist (People Ops + Hiring Manager):
1. Complete new-hire paperwork and legal forms.
2. Provision laptop and arrange shipping.
3. Create accounts: corporate email, Slack, Okta, GitHub, Notion/Confluence access.
4. Add to team calendar invites and announce on #welcome channel.

Week 1 (orientation) — Manager to do:
1. 30/60/90 expectations meeting: align on success metrics for first 90 days.
2. Team introductions & architecture overview session.
3. Assign a peer buddy for day-to-day questions.
4. Schedule: onboarding doc walkthrough, security training, and required compliance modules.

30/60/90 ramp plan (suggested):
- 30 days: complete orientation, setup local dev environment, and land first small ticket.
- 60 days: contribute meaningful features, attend design reviews, and take ownership of a small component.
- 90 days: lead a project or feature to completion, demonstrate cross-team coordination.

Hiring process summary (interviews):
- Recruiter screen → hiring manager technical/role screen → 2–3 loop interviews (technical/problem solving, systems design, and culture/additive teamwork) → bar-raiser panel/exec review for senior roles → offer.

Interview hygiene & scorecard guidance: Interviewers must complete the scorecard within 48 hours. Responsibilities:
- Recruiter: coordinate schedule and candidate experience.
- Hiring manager: own final hiring decision (in consultation with panel and people-ops).

Offer approvals & compensation bands: Bands are maintained in the Compensation playbook. Managers must route offers through People Ops for sign-off and equity allocation.

=== Internal tools & quick access guide ===

Primary systems and owners (short list):
- Identity & SSO: Okta — owner: Security Team. Use SSO to access all corporate apps.
- Source control: GitHub Enterprise — owner: Eng DX. New repos requested via GitHub repo request form.
- Ticketing & ITSM: ServiceNow (People Ops, IT tickets) — owner: People Ops. Submit onboarding and equipment tickets here.
- Confluence & Notion: Confluence is the canonical internal docs site; Notion used for some team playbooks — owner: Eng DX.
- Slack: primary communication — owner: Eng DX. Channels: #announcements, #infra, #platform, team channels.
- CI/CD: Buildkite — owner: Eng Infra. Pipelines documented in eng-infra repo.
- Observability & logs: Datadog (metrics/traces) and Loki/Fluent — owner: Eng Platform.
- Secrets & keys: HashiCorp Vault (cloud) / KMS integrations for Private customers — owner: Security.

Common procedures (commands & steps):
- Request GitHub repo: open the GitHub repo request form (link on the Eng DX Confluence page) and include repo name, team owner, and initial collaborators.
- SSH key upload: Add your SSH key to GitHub by navigating to Settings → SSH and GPG keys → New SSH key.
- Okta app access: If an app is missing, request via ITSM with "Okta app access" in the subject line; include justification and manager approval.
- Requesting cloud project access: Use the Cloud Access request template in ServiceNow — include project name, GCP/AWS account, and required roles (minimum-privilege principle).

Security & required trainings (first 30 days):
- Mandatory security onboarding: secure-coding fundamentals, phishing awareness, and data handling.
- MFA: Enforce MFA via Okta; Security will contact for device enrollment if needed.
- Secrets handling: Never store credentials in source control; use Vault and follow the Secrets Handling Policy (linked).

Escalation & support contacts:
- IT / equipment issues: submit ServiceNow ticket; People Ops IT on-call: it-oncall@redwood.com.
- Access delays: Escalate via #eng-dx-slack or email eng-dx@redwood.com with subject line "Access Delay: <hire-name>".
- Emergency / security incidents: follow the Incident Response runbook (Security & Compliance space) and call the on-call number listed there.

=== Manager checklist (first 90 days) ===
- Day 0: confirm laptop delivery, introductory email, and Slack welcome.
- Day 1: 1:1 with new hire, assign buddy, and walkthrough role responsibilities.
- Week 1–2: schedule architecture + payroll + benefits orientation.
- Month 1: review 30-day goals and remove blockers.
- Month 2: check progress against 60-day milestones, recommend learning resources.
- Month 3: finalize 90-day review and identify next objectives.

=== Frequently asked questions ===
Q: Who do I contact for payroll or benefits questions?
A: Benefits and payroll inquiries go to people-ops@redwood.com or submit a ServiceNow ticket.

Q: How do I request an ergonomic chair?
A: Submit an equipment request in ServiceNow and tag your manager for approval; standard fulfillment time is 7–10 business days.

Q: Where are the career ladders documented?
A: See the Career Ladders page in the People Ops space: /confluence/people-ops/career-ladders.
